transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I guess the main reason I came in is that I just get pulled off track so easily. Like, I'll be working on something—lately it's been this dashboard I was supposed to be finishing for my major. I'm getting my bachelor's right now, and the data visualization class is actually really cool. We use this software that makes everything look like a giant color-coded map, which I love because I've always been super visual. I actually used to paint a lot in high school, mostly acrylics, and I kind of miss it, but I don't really have the space for a canvas in my apartment... 

Wait, sorry, anyway. I'll be trying to finish the dashboard, and then I'll get one Slack ping from a classmate, or I'll hear a specific song lyric and have to go look up the meaning on Genius, or I just get a random idea for a totally different project. And then suddenly I've completely lost the thread of what I was actually supposed to be doing. So, yeah, that's mostly why I'm here.
Would you say this kind of getting easily sidetracked has been a lifelong pattern for you, going back to childhood, or is this something that's developed more recently?

Oh, definitely lifelong. Like, even way back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing comments on my report cards about me rushing through worksheets. Which, honestly, those worksheets were so boring, except for those timed math tests. I actually still have a little graphite mark on my hand from a pencil during one of those. My friend Chloe accidentally stabbed me with it—she moved to Texas in middle school, which was super sad because she had this amazing trampoline in her backyard with a sprinkler attached to it, and we used to spend all summer on it... 

Wait, sorry. What was I saying? Right, school. So my teachers said I rushed, and that I was always losing track of directions, or talking over my classmates during group work. It was a whole thing. And at home, my parents literally used to have to sit right beside me while I did my homework. Usually at the kitchen island while my mom was cooking. She makes this really incredible French onion soup, with the thick bread and melted gruyere on top? It's so good, especially when it's raining. But yeah, she’d be trying to cook and having to watch me like a hawk because I would just wander off into the living room, or I'd start a totally different activity before I even finished the first assignment. So, yeah, it's been happening for a really long time.
Growing up, did you ever get in trouble for things like fighting, breaking rules, lying, stealing, or being defiant toward authority figures like teachers or parents?

No, not really. I mean, I wasn't a bad kid or anything. I never got into fights or stole things. I was mostly just... there. Honestly, I was pretty terrified of getting in trouble. My dad was pretty strict about rules, especially curfew. He had this weird rule that we had to be home before the streetlights came on, which is so arbitrary, right? Like, in the summer, that's super late, but in the winter, it's pitch black by 5 PM. I remember one time it snowed really hard, and we were out sledding on this huge hill behind the middle school. We used those cheap plastic saucer sleds that always crack in the middle, but they go so fast. Anyway, we lost track of time because it was already dark, and when I got home, he was so mad. 

But no, I never did anything like, actually bad. I wasn't defiant or anything. I just talked too much and got distracted a lot.
Do you often feel physically restless, like needing to fidget, get up and move around, or feel like you can't sit still for long periods?

Yeah, definitely. It's like... if I'm stuck in a long Zoom lecture or trying to just sit quietly and study, I get this weird, uncomfortable pressure building up inside me. Like my body is just screaming at me to get up and pace around, or at least do something with my hands. I actually bought this pack of those little squishy mochi fidget toys off Amazon a few weeks ago to try and help. They're shaped like little animals? I got a cat one, a bunny, and this little seal that's really cute. But they get dirty so fast, like every piece of dust in my apartment just sticks to them. I tried washing them in the sink with dish soap, but then they get all weird and sticky, and you have to put baby powder on them to make them soft again. Which I didn't have, so I tried using cornstarch, and it just made a huge mess all over the bathroom counter. My roommate was kind of annoyed about it, which is fair, but she leaves her hair in the drain all the time, so... 

Oh, wait. What were we talking about? Right, sitting still. Yeah, I just can't do it for very long without feeling like I need to move or mess with something.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers or comments before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in lines or discussions?

Yeah, I do that a lot, actually. Especially when I'm working on group projects for my classes. Like, if we're brainstorming and someone is talking, I'll just blurt out my idea right in the middle of their sentence. Or I'll just start adding stuff to their Figma board before they've even finished explaining what they wanted to do. Which, I love Figma. It's so much better than Adobe XD. I tried using XD for this app design project last semester, and it crashed on me like three times in one hour. I lost all my progress on this really cool onboarding animation I was making. It had these little bouncing dots that transitioned into the logo, which took forever to keyframe perfectly. I ended up having to stay up until like 4 AM to redo it, and I drank so much Red Bull that I was vibrating the next day during my 8 AM lecture. The professor was this super old guy who talked so slow, I thought I was going to lose my mind. 

But um, anyway, yeah. I can tell afterward that I came off as pushy when I interrupt people like that, even though I'm really just excited about the project. I just get so into it and the thought is right there, and I feel like I have to say it or do it right that second before I forget.

Would you say these struggles with focus, restlessness, and interrupting have caused real problems in more than one area of your life—like your schoolwork, relationships, or job performance—not just an occasional annoyance?

Yeah, I mean, it definitely causes real problems. Like, I do a little bit of freelance graphic design on the side—mostly just small stuff for local businesses or student organizations—and I've actually lost a couple of contracts because I just couldn't follow through cleanly. I'd miss a deadline or forget to reply to an email, or I'd get halfway through a logo design and then get totally sidetracked by redesigning my own personal website instead. Which, by the way, I spent like three days coding this really cool dark mode toggle switch from scratch using CSS and JavaScript. It has this little sun and moon icon that physically rotates when you click it, and the background fades instead of just snapping to black. It was so satisfying to get it working perfectly, but then I realized I hadn't even started the actual client work I was supposed to be doing. 

And then there was this big portfolio competition last semester that I totally missed out on because I just couldn't get my stuff organized in time. It's frustrating because my friends and the people I collaborate with, they always say they love my ideas, but I can tell they get hesitant to work with me now. Like, they know I'm probably going to drop the ball on the boring organizational stuff or talk over them during meetings. So yeah, it's definitely more than just a little annoying. It's actually kind of messing things up for me.
